title: SLO Choreography: Design Lab & Cross-team Collaboration Canvas
content:
Purpose and framing:
This doc is a lightweight design-lab canvas for testing new ways of defining, operating, and handing off SLOs across product, serving runtime, and platform teams. The goal is not a final playbook but a set of reproducible experiments and a shared decision surface so partners can weigh tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs availability) for model-serving workloads.

Context/why now:
- Increasing platform complexity (hosted + dedicated + private) means SLOs must span different failure domains and fallbacks.
- We keep seeing friction during launch handoffs: product owners want optimistic SLOs, infra wants conservative error budgets.
- This lab aims to create a repeatable workshop flow and a set of artifacts teams can reuse for future feature launches.

Scope (what this canvas covers):
- SLO design for: text generation API (v1), embeddings pipeline, and routing/fallback behavior when a model variant is unavailable.
- Cross-functional actors: Product, Eng (serving-runtime), Eng (platform), Observability, Customer Success, SRE oncall.
- Outputs: 2 canonical SLOs per service, acceptance criteria for rollouts, rollout triggers, and three small experiments to validate assumptions.

Core principles (shared language):
- SLOs = commitments + operating policy (not just a number).
- Error budget is a shared currency; use it to coordinate feature ramps, not punish teams.
- Surface cost/latency tradeoffs alongside SLOs in every decision (tokens, batching, cache).

Roles & responsibilities (lab-specific):
- SLO Owner (Product): define user-facing commitment and acceptable degradation modes.
- Runtime SME (serving-runtime): provide realistic tail-latency and load profiles; propose conservative gating values.
- Platform SME: map infrastructure capacity and fallback variants; provide capacity runbook.
- Observability Lead: define signals, dashboards, alert runbooks, and evaluation prompt set.
- SRE Liaison: translate SLO into oncall runbook and escalation matrix.

Workshop rhythm (90-minute template):
1) 10m - Context + success criteria. Ask: what failure modes are most critical to users?
2) 20m - Data walk: runtime SME presents p95/p99 for last 30 days, token cost trends, cache hit rates.
3) 20m - Draft SLOs together (two buckets: availability and quality/latency).
4) 20m - Decide rollout policy: canary thresholds, error budget usage, automatic fallback mapping.
5) 15m - Experiment selection + immediate next steps (owners, tickets).

Example candidate SLOs (templates to copy and adapt):
- Service availability (user-facing): "99.9% of generation requests must return a non-error response within 800ms at steady-state traffic, measured over a rolling 30d window."
- Tail-cost SLO (cost guardrail): "Median token compute cost per request must not increase >15% during a 7d canary unless overridden by product with documented tradeoffs."
- Cache-hit SLO (performance optimization): "KV prefix cache hit-rate >= 65% during normal workloads; if hit-rate drops below 50% for 24 hours, trigger ops review."
- Quality guard (domain-specific): "Prompt set regression: >=95% of golden prompts must match baseline output pass-rates (as measured by eval harness) across model rollouts."

Decision triggers and automated actions (examples):
- If p99 latency > 1.5x baseline for 3 consecutive 1h windows -> automatic traffic shift to compatible variant with documented quality delta.
- If error budget burn rate > 2x expected during canary -> abort rollout and open cross-team incident review.

Mini-experiments (3x quick tests, each 2–4 weeks):
1) Latency-windowed canary: only route small percentage of traffic during peak p95 windows; measure user impact & cost delta.
2) Error-budget-preserving cache: enable aggressive prefix caching for 10% of requests and measure cache hit / quality drift.
3) Cost-safety gate: introduce a pre-flight cost-estimator that rejects model variants exceeding per-request cost thresholds during non-critical traffic periods.

Acceptance criteria (for calling an experiment successful):
- Clear statistical signal (pre/post) for metrics we care about (p95, p99, error-rate, cost-per-token).
- No customer-facing incidents attributable to the experiment during the test window.
- Runbook and rollback path documented and tested in staging.

Risk matrix (quick heatmap):
- User-visible latency regressions: High impact, Medium likelihood during model swaps. Mitigation: phased canary and automatic fallback.
- Cost spike: Medium impact, Low-Medium likelihood when quantization/variant changes. Mitigation: cost SLOs + pre-flight estimator.
- Observability blind spots: High impact, Medium likelihood. Mitigation: add synthetic checks & prompt-set evals before rollout.

Artifacts to produce from a lab run (templates):
- SLO spec doc (title, owner, exact metric, window, measurement source).
- Rollout policy one-pager (canary %, thresholds, automatic actions).
- Evaluation prompt set & baseline results (CSV + short analysis).
- Ops rollback runbook (play-by-play).

Handoff checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] SLO spec committed in SLO registry (link).
- [ ] Dashboards created and verified in staging with synthetic traffic.
- [ ] Acceptance criteria met in canary & experiments.
- [ ] Oncall runbook written and smoke tests passing.
- [ ] Customer Success informed of expected degradation modes and communication plan.

Postmortem cadence and learning capture:
- Small incident during lab -> 72h learning note (not a full postmortem unless severity > P2).
- Successful lab run -> 1 pager with key metrics and recommended default SLO ranges for similar services.

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (to capture during the first lab):
- Should cost-based SLOs be enforced lifecycle-wide or only during non-peak / test windows?
- How do we incentivize product teams to accept conservative error budgets early in the launch?
- Which owner has final sign-off for automatic fallback triggers (product or platform)?

Immediate next steps (ownered tickets):
- Marcus: create experiment scaffold in repo (github:repo/redwood-infra/pull/1372) -> track in JIRA SRE-9124.
- Jordan: assemble evaluation prompt set and baseline runs (linked artifact + staging job).
- Aisha: schedule first 90-minute design lab with Product (Gen API owners) week of 2026-03-08.
- Elena: draft SLO spec template and SLO-registry PR.

Notes to self / lab tips (informal):
- Keep the first workshop pragmatic: pick 1 owner and 1 measurable SLO, get it onto dashboards, and do a tiny canary.
- Prefer a conservative default if data is sparse; you can relax SLOs after you gather evidence.
- Record the workshop and clip the data-walk section for asynchronous partners.

Appendix: quick SLO spec template (copyable)
- name: string
- owner: name + team
- metric: detailed definition (source, query, labels)
- window: rolling duration
- target: numeric target and rationale
- measurement: source and retention
- alerting: who, when (soft/hard), runbook link
- rollback: immediate action mapping

End of canvas.

Footnote: this is intentionally experimental. We want a minimal, repeatable set of artifacts teams can reproduce without a heavy process overhead. Capture feedback in #sre-choreography and we'll iterate the canvas after the first two lab runs.
